source_text: וַֽ/נַּעֲבֹ֞ר מֵ/אֵ֧ת אַחֵ֣י/נוּ בְנֵי עֵשָׂ֗ו הַ/יֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּ/שֵׂעִ֔יר מִ/דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ הָֽ/עֲרָבָ֔ה מֵ/אֵילַ֖ת וּ/מֵ/עֶצְיֹ֣ן גָּ֑בֶר וַ/נֵּ֨פֶן֙ וַֽ/נַּעֲבֹ֔ר דֶּ֖רֶךְ מִדְבַּ֥ר מוֹאָֽב־ס׃
english_snapshot: So we passed on from our brothers[a], the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, away from the way of the Arabah, from Elath and from Ezion-geber[b]; and we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

signals.text: Or 'from the road of the Arabah.' 'Arabah' refers to the rift-valley region south of the Dead Sea.

source_text: וְ/הָֽ/עֲרָבָ֖ה וְ/הַ/יַּרְדֵּ֣ן וּ/גְבֻ֑ל מִ/כִּנֶּ֗רֶת וְ/עַ֨ד יָ֤ם הָֽ/עֲרָבָה֙ יָ֣ם הַ/מֶּ֔לַח תַּ֛חַת אַשְׁדֹּ֥ת הַ/פִּסְגָּ֖ה מִזְרָֽחָ/ה׃
english_snapshot: also the Arabah[a], with the Jordan as its border, from Kinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea[b], below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.

source_text: וְ/כָל הָ֨/עֲרָבָ֜ה עֵ֤בֶר הַ/יַּרְדֵּן֙ מִזְרָ֔חָ/ה וְ/עַ֖ד יָ֣ם הָ/עֲרָבָ֑ה תַּ֖חַת אַשְׁדֹּ֥ת הַ/פִּסְגָּֽה־׃פ
english_snapshot: and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan eastward[a], as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.

signals.text: That is, the body of water commonly identified as the Dead Sea.

source_text: וְ/עֹ֥שֶׂה חֶ֖סֶד לַֽ/אֲלָפִ֑ים לְ/אֹהֲבַ֖/י וּ/לְ/שֹׁמְרֵ֥י מצות/ו׃ס
english_snapshot: but showing steadfast love to thousands[a], to those who love me and keep my commandments.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and translations read 'my commandments,' which fits the surrounding first-person speech; the Hebrew text provided here reads 'his commandments.'

source_text: אֵ֣ת כָּל הַ/דָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָנֹכִי֙ מְצַוֶּ֣ה אֶתְ/כֶ֔ם אֹת֥/וֹ תִשְׁמְר֖וּ לַ/עֲשׂ֑וֹת לֹא תֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֔י/ו וְ/לֹ֥א תִגְרַ֖ע מִמֶּֽ/נּוּ־־׃פ
english_snapshot: Every word that I am commanding you[a], you shall be careful to do. You shall not add to it[b], and you shall not take away from it.

signals.text: In some English versifications, this verse is numbered as Deuteronomy 12:32.

source_text: וְ/הָיָה֮ בְּ/עָבְרְ/כֶ֣ם אֶת הַ/יַּרְדֵּן֒ תָּקִ֜ימוּ אֶת הָ/אֲבָנִ֣ים הָ/אֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֜י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְ/כֶ֛ם הַ/יּ֖וֹם בְּ/הַ֣ר עֵיבָ֑ל וְ/שַׂדְתָּ֥ אוֹתָ֖/ם בַּ/שִּֽׂיד־־׃
english_snapshot: And when you cross the Jordan[a], you shall set up these stones, which I am commanding you today, on Mount Ebal, and you shall plaster them with lime.

signals.text: Some textual traditions, notably the Samaritan Pentateuch, read “Mount Gerizim” instead of “Mount Ebal.”

source_text: בְּ/הַנְחֵ֤ל עֶלְיוֹן֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם בְּ/הַפְרִיד֖/וֹ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָ֑ם יַצֵּב֙ גְּבֻלֹ֣ת עַמִּ֔ים לְ/מִסְפַּ֖ר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
english_snapshot: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance[a], when he separated the sons of man[b], he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.

signals.text: Dead Sea Scrolls and the Septuagint read 'sons of God' (or 'angels of God') instead of 'sons of Israel.'

source_text: הַרְנִ֤ינוּ גוֹיִם֙ עַמּ֔/וֹ כִּ֥י דַם עֲבָדָ֖י/ו יִקּ֑וֹם וְ/נָקָם֙ יָשִׁ֣יב לְ/צָרָ֔י/ו וְ/כִפֶּ֥ר אַדְמָת֖/וֹ עַמּֽ/וֹ־׃פ
english_snapshot: Rejoice[a], O nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants; he will repay vengeance on his adversaries[d][c][b], and he will make atonement for his land and his people.

signals.text: The Greek Septuagint and a Dead Sea Scroll preserve a longer form of this verse, including additional calls for the heavens and divine beings to rejoice and for the nations to worship him. The main text here follows the Masoretic Hebrew.
